dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: indriyadvārakaṃ sarvaṃ sukhaduḥkhādisaṃgamam | itīndriyāṇi saṃtyajya svasthaḥ svātmani vartate ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: All contact with pleasure, pain and the rest comes through the doors of the senses; knowing this, letting go of the senses, one abides at ease in one's own Self.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: pleasure and pain received through the senses belong not to the essential Self but to the psycho-physical complex; this is achieved mainly by śakti-saṃkoca, which the Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya defines as turning back toward the Self the consciousness spreading outward through the senses. One becomes poised in oneself (svastha), free of the opposites. He cites the Yogavāsiṣṭha. Singh classes it as śāktopāya. Wallis: 'abide in oneself'; let go of attachment to the senses and be at ease in the natural state.
dharana.technique_name: Pleasure and Pain Come Through the Senses: Abiding in Oneself
dharana.instruction: Notice that pleasure and pain come through the senses, and let attention turn back to rest at ease within.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 111' = verse 136 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 136 = 'Abide in oneself (Y110 ~ C3)' (verse text and technique match)

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 136 'Dharana 113', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 111. Not followed.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 136 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: pleasure and pain arriving through them
attention turned back to rest in oneself
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the senses as doors through which pleasure and pain arrive, and attention turning back from the doors to rest at home.
geometry.svg_hint: a simple house outline with open doors and windows, and a soft light at its centre
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Come home
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: attention that keeps going out through the senses toward pleasure and pain turns back and rests at ease within. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Let attention turn back from the senses and rest within
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The recognition that pleasure and pain arrive through the senses
attention.secondary: Attention resting at ease in oneself, not reaching out through them

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: All contact with pleasure, pain and the rest comes through the doors of the senses; knowing this, letting go of the senses, one abides at ease in one's own Self.
adiyogi.method_summary: Notice that every pleasant or unpleasant experience arrives through a sense: seeing, hearing, touch, taste, smell. Without closing anything off, let attention stop reaching out through those doors and turn back. Rest, at ease, in yourself.

honesty.disclosure: Door 111 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 111 (verse 136) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 111 is dharana 111, verse 136. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. This is not ignoring pain that needs care, and it is not cutting off from the world; it is resting attention within for a while. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
